mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that supports corporate profit growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.0, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is negative and statistically insignificant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 3.0% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 3.0%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is positive but statistically insignificant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3.0% and unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals dual stress on monetary policy and labor market conditions, compressing corporate earnings growth and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% AND UNRATE > 4.0%, or the rank correlation between the joint condition and returns is positive but statistically insignificant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market expansion regime (HOUST above 1600 thousand units), strong housing activity supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above 1600, or the rank correlation between HOUST and 20-day returns is positive but statistically insignificant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 5-day returns is positive but statistically insignificant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL level above 295 (indicating annualized inflation exceeding 5% from the 1982-1984 base) signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL is above 295, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 60-day returns is negative but statistically insignificant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average, or the rank correlation between RSAFS and 20-day returns is positive but statistically insignificant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate below 3.5% indicates a tight labor market that fuels wage growth and consumer spending, boosting corporate earnings and stock valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 5-day returns is negative but statistically insignificant (p>0.05).
